issues.claim: SQL Server keeps its previous committed version in the version store (usually in `tempdb`).
issues.problem: With Accelerated Database Recovery enabled (the default in Azure SQL Database), the persistent version store lives in the user database, not in tempdb. The word 'usually' covers this, but the exception is not stated.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: 'in the version store (in tempdb, or in the persistent version store of the user database when Accelerated Database Recovery is on)'. Apply the same change to the RU text.

issues.claim: The `READCOMMITTEDLOCK` hint restores the locking behavior for a single query.
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt is cut off at 'READCOMMITTE...'. The claim is correct (SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL and the table hints docs document READCOMMITTEDLOCK), but the excerpt does not show it in full.
issues.suggestedFix: No content change needed. Optionally add the table hints page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/queries/hints-transact-sql-table) as a source.

issues.claim: Так ведёт себя `READ COMMITTED` на блокировках, когда параметр выключен.
issues.problem: The phrasing is slightly awkward Russian.
issues.suggestedFix: Так ведёт себя `READ COMMITTED`, основанный на блокировках, когда параметр выключен.

issues.claim: In EF Core with `EnableRetryOnFailure`, the SQL Server provider strategy treats error 1205 as transient, but an explicit transaction must then run inside `Database.CreateExecutionStrategy().ExecuteAsync(...)`.
issues.problem: The claim is correct (SqlServerTransientExceptionDetector includes 1205), but neither cited link supports it. Both are SQL Server pages and say nothing about EF Core.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the EF Core connection resiliency page as a third link (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ef/core/miscellaneous/connection-resiliency), with matching linkTitles in both locales.

issues.claim: whether it is a conversion deadlock (both sessions read with S and then update)
issues.problem: Under the default READ COMMITTED level without RCSI, S locks on rows are released right after the read. A conversion deadlock therefore needs REPEATABLE READ, HOLDLOCK or SERIALIZABLE, or a read inside a transaction that holds the S lock. The text implies it can happen under defaults.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: 'whether it is a conversion deadlock (both sessions hold S locks, for example under REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE or with HOLDLOCK, and then try to upgrade to X)'. Apply the same change to the RU text.
